chunks.title: Project: Geospatial Segmentation
chunks.text: Geospatial Segmentation (Deep learning · Research). Mapping how land changes over time, pixel by pixel, from paired satellite images. 4,662 image pairs, 512² pixels per image, 7 land classes, IEEE Xplore paper. Goals: See change, not just land: How might two images of the same place show exactly what changed between them? Handle uneven classes: How might a model stay accurate when some land classes are much rarer than others? Experiments you can repeat: How might every training run be named, versioned and reproducible?
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: Geospatial Segmentation: how it works
chunks.text: Dual-input segmentation: Change only shows up when both dates are looked at together. Both images go into one U-Net, stacked as 6 input channels. The model outputs two 3-class masks, one for each date. Pixel-wise differencing of the masks highlights where land changed. Trade-off: About 31M parameters, a 120 MB model and 2–8 GB of GPU memory. Training at scale: Thousands of 512 × 512 image pairs are too heavy for a simple training loop. Mixed precision with gradient scaling for faster GPU training. Focal loss to handle class imbalance. Warm-restart cosine scheduling, with early stopping after 10 flat epochs. Checkpoints every 10 epochs, so training can resume. Trade-off: A full run still takes 2–8 hours on a GPU. Config-driven runs: Editing scripts by hand makes runs hard to compare. Every parameter lives in a YAML file. Experiments are named and versioned. A quick-test config trains on 20 images for 5 epochs. Trade-off: More configuration to keep in sync than a single script.
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: Geospatial Segmentation: Dataset
chunks.text: --- --- Training pairs 2,968 Test pairs 1,694 Image size 512 × 512 RGB Classes 3 (pixel values 0, 128, 255 → 0, 1, 2) Task Dual-output semantic segmentation Each sample is a pair of input images ( im1 , im2 ) with a segmentation mask for each ( label1 , label2 ).

chunks.title: Geospatial Segmentation: Model
chunks.text: An enhanced dual-input U-Net: - Input: 6 channels (two 3-channel RGB images stacked) - Output: two 3-class segmentation masks - Encoder: 64 → 128 → 256 → 512, with a 1024-channel bottleneck - Skip connections, batch normalisation, ReLU and dropout - Attention mechanisms in the full-dataset model - About 31M parameters (~120 MB of weights)

Techniques - Focal loss to handle class imbalance - Mixed precision training with gradient scaling - CosineAnnealingWarmRestarts learning-rate schedule with the AdamW optimiser - Early stopping (patience of 10 epochs) and checkpoints every 10 epochs - Augmentation: horizontal and vertical flips, ±15° rotation, colour jitter, applied identically to images and masks - Automatic batch size (2–16, from GPU memory), memory pinning and non-blocking transfers: 2–4× faster on GPU Config-driven experiments Every parameter lives in a YAML file, so experiments are named, versioned and reproducible:

chunks.title: Project: ScriptSync
chunks.text: ScriptSync (Video translation · Languages). Translates a whole video, from the words on screen to the voice, into another language. 60% faster processing, 150+ languages, 1st VIT YANTRA Central Hackathon. Goals: Text in the frame too: How might text burned into the video be translated and redrawn in place? Skip what hasn’t changed: How might the pipeline avoid running OCR on frames whose text is the same? Dub the voice: How might speech be transcribed, translated and spoken again in the new language?
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: ScriptSync: how it works
chunks.text: On-screen text: Subtitles miss text that’s part of the picture itself. GPU-accelerated OCR finds the text in each frame. The translation is drawn back over the original text. Fuzzy text matching reuses translations for near-identical text. A thread-safe cache shares results across workers. Trade-off: Redrawn text can’t match every original font exactly. Frame differencing: OCR on every frame is the slowest part of the pipeline. Each frame is compared with the last one processed. Only frames that changed past a threshold go to OCR. A cap on consecutive skips keeps the text from drifting. Multithreaded workers, with a limit on concurrent GPU jobs. Trade-off: Set the threshold too high and small text changes can be missed. Audio dubbing: A translated picture with the original voice still isn’t watchable. faster-whisper transcribes the speech. NLLB-200 translates the transcript. MMS-TTS speaks it in the target language. FFmpeg joins the new video and audio into the final MP4. Trade-off: The first run has to download the model weights.
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: ScriptSync: What the pipeline does
chunks.text: 1. Translates on-screen text with the multithreaded video pipeline. 2. Extracts the source audio from the input video. 3. Transcribes speech with faster-whisper . 4. Translates the transcript with NLLB ( facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M ). 5. Synthesises dubbed speech with MMS-TTS ( facebook/mms-tts- ). 6. Muxes the translated video and dubbed audio into the final MP4.
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: ScriptSync: Speed and quality
chunks.text: - Use a GPU for the best speed with --device cuda , or --device auto when CUDA is available. - Frame differencing skips frames whose text hasn't changed, so only new text goes through OCR.

chunks.title: Project: Mindgarden
chunks.text: Mindgarden (Full stack · Knowledge graph). A calm, private place to capture notes and watch your ideas connect. 3 import & export formats, 0 external AI services, Offline drafts that sync. Goals: Capture without friction: How might writing a note feel as quick as having the thought? Make connections visible: How might related notes find each other? Keep it yours: How might notes stay private, portable and usable offline?
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: Mindgarden: how it works
chunks.text: Graph explorer: A list of notes hides how the ideas relate. Notes are nodes and connections are edges, drawn with React Flow. The graph is grouped and coloured by tag. Search and tag filters narrow what’s on screen. Trade-off: Big graphs get dense, so filters do a lot of the work. Connections: Ideas grow when they’re linked, not when they sit in folders. Tags, named relationships and backlinks between notes. Related-note suggestions and quick summaries. Suggestions are generated locally, without an external AI service. Trade-off: Local suggestions are simpler than a hosted model, but nothing leaves the server. Safe and portable: Notes are only useful if you can trust that they’ll still be there. Version history you can restore from. Local drafts that sync when you reconnect. Markdown, CSV and JSON import and export. Read-only sharing with other accounts, revocable at any time. Trade-off: Offline drafts stay on one device until it reconnects.
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: Mindgarden: What you can do
chunks.text: - Capture: write in Markdown, start from a template, and drafts save as you type. - Connect: tags, named relationships, backlinks and related-note suggestions. - Grow: explore notes in a searchable graph, grouped and coloured by tag.
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: Mindgarden: Features
chunks.text: - Stay organised with search, related-term matching, tag filters, sorting, pins, archive and trash. - Pick up where you left off with daily notes, reminders and version history you can restore. - Keep ideas portable with Markdown, CSV and JSON import and export, plus file attachments. - Work offline with local drafts that sync when you reconnect. - Share selectively with read-only access for other Mindgarden accounts, revocable at any time. - Get a little perspective from quick summaries and related-idea suggestions, generated locally without an external AI service.

chunks.title: Project: Afterword
chunks.text: Afterword (Full stack · Generative AI). Catch up on any episode in a minute: pick a show, choose an episode, read a short recap. Gemini writes the recaps, 3+ API containers, Redis shared cache. Goals: A recap for any episode: How might a short recap be ready for any show, season and episode? Fast the second time: How might popular recaps avoid being regenerated for every user? Grow without surprises: How might the API scale across containers with shared limits?
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: Afterword: how it works
chunks.text: AI recaps: Catching up on a show shouldn’t mean rewatching it. Google Gemini writes each recap on the server. TMDB powers show search and popular shows. API keys live only on the server, never in the browser. Trade-off: Every new recap costs a model call, which is why caching matters. Accounts & history: Recaps are worth keeping once you’ve read them. Google sign-in with OAuth 2.0. OAuth state and login cookies are signed with HMAC. Saved recaps are stored in PostgreSQL under each account. Guests can generate recaps without signing in. Trade-off: Guest recaps skip the cache, so they’re always generated fresh. Built to scale: One server falls over the moment a recap gets popular. Docker Compose runs the full stack. Traefik load-balances across backend containers. Redis is a shared cache and rate limiter for every instance. HTTPS with Let’s Encrypt for public deploys. Trade-off: A deleted recap stays in the shared cache until it expires.
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: Afterword: How it works
chunks.text: - Show search and popular shows come from the TMDB API, called from the server so the key never reaches the browser. - Recaps are generated server-side with Google Gemini. - Signed-in recaps are cached by show, season and episode, and saved in PostgreSQL under the Google account. - Guest recaps skip the cache entirely and aren't saved. - Deleting a saved recap removes it from that account's history; the shared cache entry expires on its own TTL.
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: Afterword: Architecture
chunks.text: Layer What it does --- --- Frontend React.js and TypeScript on Vite; proxies /api to the backend in development Backend Express API for search, recap generation, auth and history Cache Redis, shared by every backend instance for recap caching and rate limits Database PostgreSQL for user accounts and saved recaps Gateway Traefik routes requests and load-balances across backend containers
chunks.k: project projects built build made work portfolio

chunks.title: Afterword: Authentication
chunks.text: - Google OAuth 2.0 sign-in and sign-up. - OAuth state and login cookies are signed with an HMAC session secret. - Cookies are marked secure when served over HTTPS.

chunks.title: This website
chunks.text: The site is a 3D model of Sameer's home office. Places: the books (about, experience, education, extracurriculars), the computer (an iMac with his projects, certifications and skills), the certificate wall (achievements), the files (résumé), the phone (contact), the speaker (song picks), the camera (photos) and Rio & Bruno (his dogs).
